# chunk-engine

> One document chunking engine for RAG — 36 file formats, one Rust core, shipped as three byte-identical SDKs: py-chunks (Python), js-chunks (JavaScript/WASM), and rs-chunks (Rust). It turns any document into clean, retrieval-ready, typed chunks in a single call.

chunk-engine is a document-understanding engine (not a plain text splitter): it reads 36 file formats natively and returns typed chunks (`content_type` = heading, table, code_block, bullet_list, plain_paragraph, …) each carrying format- and section-specific `metadata`. The parsing and chunking run in a compiled Rust core; thin bindings expose the same API — and produce the same output — from Python, JavaScript, or Rust.

Install: `pip install py-chunks` · `npm install js-chunks` · `cargo add rs-chunks`.

Core API: `get_chunks(source, mode=...)` / `getChunks(source, { mode })` returns a list of `{ content, content_type, metadata }`; `stream_chunks(...)` / `streamChunks(...)` yields them lazily with constant memory; `get_markdown(...)` / `getMarkdown(...)` converts any document to a Markdown string; images come out via `list_images` / `listImages`.

Modes: document formats (DOCX, PDF, PPTX, HTML, Markdown, TXT, email, eBooks, notebooks) support `default`, `structural`, `section`, `semantic`, `sliding_window`, `sentence` and `page_aware`; spreadsheets (XLSX, XLS, ODS) support `row`, `table`, `sheet`, `sliding_window`, `page_aware` and `semantic`; delimited files (CSV, TSV) support `row`, `sliding_window` and `page_aware`.

Every link below points at the raw Markdown of a page. The human-readable HTML lives at the same path under `/docs/` instead of `/md/` — for example <https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/quick-start> renders at <https://www.chunkengine.dev/docs/quick-start>.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/index): what chunk-engine is, and how it differs from a text splitter.
- [Installation](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/installation): install for Python, JavaScript or Rust; no runtime dependencies.
- [Quick Start](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/quick-start): chunk a document, stream a large one, convert to Markdown.
- [Input Sources](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/input-sources): file path, raw bytes, file-like object, upload, presigned URL.
- [Languages & parity](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/languages): why the three SDKs return byte-identical output.

## Chunking modes

- [Chunking Modes overview](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/chunking-modes): which modes exist and which formats support them.
- [structural](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/chunking-modes/structural): the default — one chunk per structural block.
- [section](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/chunking-modes/section): group blocks under their heading.
- [semantic](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/chunking-modes/semantic): merge related blocks up to a size budget.
- [sentence](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/chunking-modes/sentence): fixed number of sentences per chunk.
- [sliding_window](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/chunking-modes/sliding-window): overlapping windows for recall.
- [page_aware](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/chunking-modes/page-aware): respect page and slide boundaries.

## Reference

- [Output Schema](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/output-schema): the chunk shape and every `content_type` value.
- [Metadata Reference](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/metadata-reference): every metadata key, per format and per mode.
- [API Reference](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/api-reference): full signatures for all three SDKs.
- [Supported Formats](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/supported-formats): the 36 extensions and what each yields.
- [Streaming](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/streaming): which modes stream, and the memory profile of each format.
- [Error Handling](https://www.chunkengine.dev/md/error-handling): the exceptions each SDK raises and when.
